register.name: Dodecanese interconnection, phase 1: EU grant
register.detail: European Commission (CINEA) · Public Sector Loan Facility · announced 16 November 2026 · phase 1 budget €2.54bn
register.note: Alongside a €1.53 billion EIB loan and a €534 million grant from the Greek Decarbonisation Fund
register.text: An EU grant for the first phase of the link joining the Dodecanese islands to the mainland grid: a High Voltage Direct Current submarine link from Corinth to Kos with two AC/DC converter stations, delivered by the Independent Power Transmission Operator (IPTO). It serves the energy standard, and the agency expects phase 1 to cut CO₂ emissions by around 7.7 million tonnes over 25 years and to create 40 permanent jobs.

register.text: An EIB loan to Piraeus Bank to on-lend to small and mid-sized firms active in agriculture and the bioeconomy, including green projects and firms that promote youth employment. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

It serves the water and shelter standards, with more drought-resilient water supply and wastewater services for more than 4 million residents.

register.name: Antonis Tritsis programme: green and sustainable urban development

register.text: An EIB loan to the Consignment Deposits and Loans Fund for hundreds of projects in Greek cities and towns: water and wastewater management, anti-seismic measures in schools, energy-efficient public buildings, waste and recycling, and climate-resilient roads. It serves the water, education and energy standards.

register.name: University of Crete student accommodation, public-private partnership

register.note: Energy-efficient student dormitories, in the EIB Group’s 2025 results for Greece

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: 12.9% are under fifteen: the workforce and the market of the next generation.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of the land under forest, 2024
items.text: Standing forest that stores carbon and water, and can earn as it stands.

items.name: The Farmland
items.label: Of the land in agriculture, 2023
items.text: Land that can feed the nation and earn abroad, valued and financed against its harvest.

items.name: The Clean Grid
items.label: Of electricity from renewable sources, 2021
items.text: Power from water, wind and sun already flows; every new connection can be clean.

items.name: The Fresh Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water a person, 2022
items.text: Rain and rivers renewed every year: power, irrigation and drinking water.

items.name: Boroume
items.text: A non-profit that matches surplus food that would otherwise go to waste with people in need, through one of the largest food aid networks in Greece. It matches an average of 24,400 meals a day with people in need and works with over 650 non-profits across the country.

items.name: Food Bank Greece
items.text: Founded in 1995 and a member of the European Food Banks Federation, it collects surplus food from supermarkets, food manufacturers and agricultural cooperatives and distributes it to charities that support households and soup kitchens. It works with 324 institutions and, with support from The Hellenic Initiative, has helped provide over 1.8 million meals to vulnerable families.

items.name: Electra Energy Cooperative
items.text: A certified social cooperative in Athens, founded in 2016, that helps citizens found and run energy communities across Greece and renovates homes for vulnerable households. Since 2025 it has been a partner in SPETE, one of the enablers of the European Commission’s Support Service for Citizen-led Renovation.

items.name: Hyperion Energy Community
items.text: A citizen energy community in Athens with 123 members and a 500 kWp solar park for self-consumption, and a founding member of the national coalition of energy communities. Its current project aims to help 20 energy-vulnerable women in Athens address energy poverty.

items.name: Shedia
items.text: Greece’s street paper, launched in Athens in March 2013 and sold by a network of 120 to 150 vendors in Athens and Thessaloniki, all direct victims of the socio-economic crisis; in 2023 it was the largest-selling Greek monthly magazine. It has added a restaurant, whose first cooks came from its vendors and social organisations, and upcycling workshops that turn unsold copies into products for sale.

dispatches.label: 16 Nov 2026
dispatches.author: steward
dispatches.title: EU awards €228.9 million grant to link the Dodecanese to Greece’s grid
dispatches.summary: On 16 November 2026 the European Commission announced a €228.9 million EU grant, paired with a €1.53 billion European Investment Bank loan, for the first phase of the subsea link joining the Dodecanese islands to the Greek mainland grid.
body: On 16 November 2026 the European Climate, Infrastructure and Environment Executive Agency (CINEA) announced that the Dodecanese islands will be connected to the Greek mainland grid with the support of a €228.9 million EU grant. The chairman of the Independent Power Transmission Operator (IPTO), which delivers the project, called it the largest grant awarded to date under this EU funding programme.

The grant comes from the Public Sector Loan Facility, part of the EU’s Just Transition Mechanism, which pairs EU grants with loans from the European Investment Bank. Phase 1 has an estimated budget of €2.54 billion: the €228.9 million EU grant, a €1.53 billion EIB loan and a €534 million grant from the Greek Decarbonisation Fund. The announcement does not state the loan’s tenor or rate, or when the grant agreement is signed.

The money finances the first of two phases of the interconnection: a High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) submarine link between the mainland at Corinth and the island of Kos, together with two AC/DC converter stations and the associated transmission infrastructure. The agency expects phase 1 alone to cut CO₂ emissions by around 7.7 million tonnes over 25 years, roughly 309,000 tonnes a year, and to create 40 permanent jobs.

It moves energy, one of the seven standards: islands that are electrically isolated today gain a link to the national grid, and the agency expects the project to replace oil-fired generation with a cleaner, more efficient electricity supply.

The structure could work for another nation. Cyprus, another island member state of the European Union, could pair an EU grant with a long-term EIB loan in the same way to finance the modernisation of its grid.
